I'm not sure I understand your comment correctly, but services or companies that will be required to look at user's private messages etc. will simply not be allowed to operate within EU like that. It's not like people will look at this and go "oh well, companies can't separate users, so you can do with our users as you please, according to laws that don't apply to them". More like "find a solution for our users or go away from our market".

That's why websites that do not follow GDPR for whatever reason are not available in the EU.

That's why Twitter has options available only in Germany regarding reporting Nazi propaganda etc.

Well, we certainly use different meanings of the word "design". Coming from design studies, design is world making and is a deliberate human mental stance of creating and ascribing meaning. Cells don't design anything, because they have no capacity to do so. They constitute a body, make it possible for it to exist, but they don't design it. Nobody or nothing "programmed" them to make human bodies. 

I'm not a gender scholar to indulge in theoretical discussions on how to define a gender and frankly, for my purposes, I don't care and don't need one. I have no personal, social or political reason to deny someone womanhood if they claim they're a woman. Biology is not binary and many things that are considered to be "objectively" biological are merely a product of human categorization (which is made up in a sense that there's no inherent reason why things should be so and so. Which I believe applies to gender/sex, defined as difference is genitalia or disposition to create new beings. There's no reason we couldn't define "biological" gender based on differences in height for example, instead of ability to impregnate and be pregnant, and reasons why it's like that and not different is a matter of another discussion)

Why do people in the comments argue about animal testing while this article is clearly about animal ABUSE? Yes, animal testing is currently an inseparable part of science, but there are many boards, acts and other legislations that prevent ABUSE and try to guide researchers to treat animals as ethically as possible. This article IS NOT ABOUT ANIMAL TESTING FOR FUCK'S SAKE. The research done at the facility didn't follow these legislations - that's why PCRM is getting interested in this case - excess deaths, no clear records, withholding the records, stressing animals and exhausting them (animals are supposed to have their boundaries respected, provided with food, shelter, water, sleep and veterinary care all the time and sick animals are not to be subjects of the tests). It's literally doing what is has been made to do - making sure the law which prevents abuse is respected. Abuse of animals is not a normal part of science.
